title: feat(spec, plugin-sharing): ownership-queue reads take the caller package, so a declared rule's queue recipient resolves by ADR-0150 D3
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9TtV9zn69iQ2y6yezQxLz2i)_

Fixes #31734

Clause-②: yes (widening); narrowing per ADR-0150 D3 declared below
Metadata-protocol: none
Narrowing (ADR-0150 D3): a declared sharing rule whose package P depends on a disabled package D, where an unrelated package U declares a queue of the same name. Before (main `43fb4822`): the rule granted to U's queue members, silently. After: the recipient is refused, `outside-closure`, naming U, logged once at `warn` (D3 never reaches U, and a disabled package holds nothing for this read); U's members gain no grant, grants the rule already holds are kept, as for any refused recipient. Pin: `refuses when the holder the caller reaches is disabled, naming the unrelated holder as outside the closure — never serving it, never silent` (ablations A4–A6). First-party: 0 (no first-party package declares a queue). Seat 3 ruled it the D3 answer.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：所有权队列服务契约（`IOwnershipQueueService`）的三个按队列名读取的方法（`resolveQueue`、`expandMembers`、`isMember`）加了一个可选的「调用方软件包」参数。共享插件在读「声明的共享规则」的队列接收方时，把规则所在的包传进去，队列就从这个包出发解析：本包的队列，否则它声明依赖的包里唯一持有者，否则拒绝并列出全部候选。不传参数时与今天完全一样。
- 为什么改：E4（#31728）落地时契约里没有调用方，只能整环境解析，所以「规则的依赖包和一个无关包都有同名队列」会被拒绝。这比 ADR-0150 D3 更严。本卡把这半补上（专题 #31527）。
- 风险与回滚：只影响「两个已安装的包声明了同名队列，且某个包里的共享规则把它当接收方」的部署。第一方实测 0 个包声明队列。另有一个边角情形（规则依赖的那个包被禁用、无关包有同名队列）：以前悄悄发给了无关包的成员，现在拒绝，日志 warn 一次，点名那个无关包。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/package-scoped-declarations.ts` 的 `resolveDeclaredName`（调用方分支）；`sharing-rule-service.ts` 的 `queueRecipientCaller`；`packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts` 的新可选键。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run src/package-scoped-declarations.test.ts`，预期 23 个用例全绿（新增 6 个）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **Contract (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`).** `resolveQueue`, `expandMembers` and `isMember` take an optional `callerPackageId` (new exported type `OwnershipQueueCallerPackage` = `string | null`). With a package id the name resolves from that package (ADR-0150 D3). Omitted, `null` or `''`, the read is environment-wide, as before. `queuesOf` and `hasAnyQueue` name no queue and take none. `declaredQueueNamed` (the activation door's lookup) is unchanged: the door belongs to no package. An implementation written before the key still satisfies the contract (pinned).
- **Resolution (`package-scoped-declarations.ts`).** `resolveDeclaredName` takes an optional caller package. With one and a registry that carries the package-scoped slice, the answer is objectql's `resolvePackageScopedName` from that package, final: no one-listed-item shortcut (the one listed item may be outside the package's reach), and no first-registered fallback. The listing still bounds it: the resolver is asked over `listedHoldersView(registry)`, which leaves out a holder whose package is disabled (the filter `listItems` applies) and changes nothing else. So a package whose one reachable holder is disabled gets the resolver's own `outside-closure` refusal naming every holder still served, never the disabled holder's item and never silence. Without a caller package nothing changes.
- **Queue service (`ownership-queue-service.ts`).** The three reads pass `callerPackageId` to that resolution. Refusals answer as E4's do: `null` / `[]` / `false`, or under `onFailedRead: 'refuse'` a `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, every candidate named), reported once per name and caller.
- **Rule service (`sharing-rule-service.ts`).** `assertQueueRecipientReachable` becomes `queueRecipientCaller`: the same P-side check (now over the same `listedHoldersView`), which still throws and reports its refusal first, and then it hands the rule's package to `isMember` / `expandMembers`. The check stays ahead of the read on purpose, so a queue service written before the key (environment-wide) can never serve a holder outside P's reach. New `queueRecipientPackageOf(rule)` answers the rule's package for a look-through that grants nothing.
- **BU look-through (`sharing-plugin.ts`).** "Does this queue recipient read the BU tree?" now resolves the rule's queue from the rule's package, so it reads the queue the grants are read from.
- **Position look-through (`queuesNaming`).** It reads every declared holder's specifications, not only the names an environment-wide read serves. Without this, a rule served by D's `q` (a name U also declares) would not be re-evaluated when a position moves in D's queue, and its grants would go stale. Including a name more often only re-evaluates a rule, which then answers as before.
- Changeset: patch for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, with both declaration lines.

## Step 0: every implementer and caller of the contract

Measured at `43fb4822` (main with E4).

| Site | Method | Caller package after this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| plugin-sharing `OwnershipQueueService` (the one registered implementation) | implements all | reads it |
| spec `ownership-queue-failed-read.pin.test.ts` `legacy` double | implements, no key | compiles unchanged (pinned) |
| plugin-sharing `sharing-rule-service.ts` (rule recompute, per-user pass) | `expandMembers`, `isMember` | **the declared rule's package** |
| plugin-sharing `sharing-plugin.ts` (BU-tree look-through) | `resolveQueue` | **the declared rule's package** |
| plugin-sharing `sharing-service.ts` (sitting-record access path) | `queuesOf`, `isMember` | none (no package asks) |
| plugin-security `authz-middleware`, `explain-access` | `isMember` | none |
| plugin-security `ownership-queue-gate.ts`, `kernel-queue-membership.ts` | `resolveQueue`, `queuesOf` | none |
| plugin-hono-server `current-user-endpoints.ts` | `hasAnyQueue` | none (takes no name) |
| runtime `catalog-activation.ts` (activation door) | `declaredQueueNamed` | none (unchanged method) |
| objectql `assignment-rules.ts` (assignment pool) | `resolveQueue`, `expandMembers` | none: see Acceptance notes |
| plugin-approvals `approval-service.ts` (approver slate) | `expandMembers` | none: see Acceptance notes |

Every caller that passes no key compiles and answers as before. Test doubles in objectql, plugin-approvals and plugin-security are untouched.

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in the E4 harness `src/package-scoped-declarations.test.ts` (6 cases, real `SchemaRegistry`):

- P = ALPHA depends on D = BETA; U = GAMMA is unrelated; BETA and GAMMA each declare queue `support`. From ALPHA, `resolveQueue` answers BETA's queue, `expandMembers` answers `['u_beta']` (also under `refuse`), `isMember` is `true` for `u_beta` and `false` for `u_gamma`. **Red on main.**
- The declared rule in ALPHA naming `support`: the standing grant to `u_beta` is still desired (`revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` returns `0`). **Red on main** (main throws the two-holder refusal).
- ALPHA depends on BETA and GAMMA, both declare `support`: refused, `ambiguous-in-closure`, candidates BETA and GAMMA, `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` under `refuse`, nothing under `nobody`.
- No caller package (`undefined`, `null`, `''`), same fixture as the first case: refused environment-wide naming BETA and GAMMA, exactly as main.
- BETA disabled: from ALPHA `resolveQueue` is `null` and `expandMembers` `[]`; under `refuse` a `409` `outside-closure` refusal naming GAMMA; the queue service warns once naming GAMMA; the declared rule's recompute throws the same refusal and the rule service warns naming GAMMA. **Red on main** (main serves GAMMA's members, silently).
- `queuesNaming('position', …)` finds `support` from either holder's position. **Red on main.**

Forced test change: `packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-failed-read.pin.test.ts` pinned the exact option keys (`_ExpandOptionKeys`, `_IsMemberOptionKeys`); both now include `callerPackageId`. The file gains a second `describe` with the new key's type pins. No other existing test was edited.

## Acceptance notes

- **Claim's "only the D-and-U case moves".** Measured by running the new block against main's plugin source (`git restore --source=43fb4822` on the four source files, then restored, `git diff HEAD` empty): 5 of the 6 new cases are red on main, 18 of 23 in the file green. The D-and-U case moves from refused to resolved, as the card asks. Two other cases also move, and both are declared here for the seat:
  - **A disabled dependency.** P depends on D, D is disabled, U holds the same queue name. Main serves U's queue to P's rule, silently (the P-side check passes through D, then the environment-wide listing sees only U). This PR refuses it, naming U as outside P's closure, and reports it. That is a narrowing of a wrong answer, first-party count 0 (no first-party package declares a queue). Seat 3 accepted it as the D3 answer; the epic seat asked that it be reported, naming U; declared on the `Narrowing` line above and in the changeset.
  - **The position look-through.** It now includes names two packages declare. A rule naming such a name re-evaluates on a position write; for a rule with no package that re-evaluation answers the refusal it already answers on every other recompute (its grants are kept and it warns), so the visible difference is that warning on one more path.
  - The two-holders-in-closure case refuses on both trees; only the refusal's vocabulary moves (`ambiguous-in-environment` with no caller on main, `ambiguous-in-closure` naming ALPHA here). Same candidates, same `409`.
- **Other package-written queue references.** A declared assignment rule's queue (objectql `assignment-rules.ts`) and an approval step's queue (plugin-approvals) are also written inside a package and still read environment-wide. That is stricter than D3, never looser, the same interim E4 accepted for this card. Outside this card's file surface; carrier: epic #31527 seat.
- **New public name** `OwnershipQueueCallerPackage` and the option key `callerPackageId` (the resolver's own `PackageScopedQuery` key). The seat's call.

  - A4, the caller-package refusal silenced (answered `not-found`): 2 red, `refuses when the caller's closure reaches two holders …` and `refuses when the holder the caller reaches is disabled, naming the unrelated holder …`.
  - A5, `listedHoldersView` unfiltered (a disabled holder counted): 1 red, the disabled-dependency pin (the disabled holder's queue served).
  - A6, the rule service's own check over the raw registry instead of the view: 1 red, the same pin (its warning naming GAMMA missing). That is the guard that holds for a queue service written before the key.
